blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Solve the following system of linear equations by matrix inversion method: \(x - 2y + z = -1\), \(3x + y - 2z = 4\), \(y - z = 1\)
blocks.explanation:
Teen linear equations hain aur tareeqa pehle se tay hai: \(X = A^{-1}B\).
Teeno unknowns nikalne hain.
Plan: \(|A|\), phir nau (9) cofactors, \(\operatorname{adj}A\), \(A^{-1}\), phir \(B\) se zarb, aur aakhir mein tasdeeq.
Dhyan dein: \(X = A^{-1}B\) likhein, \(BA^{-1}\) nahi, kyunke matrix multiplication mein tarteeb badalne se jawab badal jata hai aur \(B\) \(3 \times 1\) hai, is liye \(BA^{-1}\) to ban hi nahi sakta. Cofactors ka sign pattern \(+ - +\), \(- + -\), \(+ - +\) yaad rakhein, aur adjoint banate waqt transpose lena na bhoolein: yeh do ghaltiyan exam mein sab se zyada hoti hain. Fraction \(\frac{1}{|A|}\) ko aakhir tak bahar rakhein, is se hisaab saaf rehta hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x - 2y + z = -1\), \(3x + y - 2z = 4\), \(y - z = 1\)
Humein find karna hai: matrix inversion method se \(x, y, z\).
Tareeqa: System ko \(AX = B\) likhenge. Agar \(|A| \neq 0\) ho to dono taraf left se \(A^{-1}\) se zarb denge: \(A^{-1}AX = A^{-1}B\), yani \(X = A^{-1}B\). Inverse ke liye formula \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A\) use karenge.

System ko \(AX = B\) ki shakal mein likhein
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix},\ B = \begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki har row ek equation ke coefficients hain. Jo variable kisi equation mein maujood na ho, us ki jagah 0 likhna zaroori hai, warna matrix ghalat ban jata hai.

\(|A|\) nikalein
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(-1 + 2) + 2(-3 - 0) + 1(3 - 0)\]
\[= 1 - 6 + 3\]
\[= -2\]
Kyun: \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, is liye \(A^{-1}\) exist karta hai aur yeh method chalega.

Row 1 ke cofactors
\[A_{11} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1 + 2) = 1\]
\[A_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix}3 & -2 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-3 - 0) = 3\]
\[A_{13} = +\begin{vmatrix}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (3 - 0) = 3\]
Kyun: \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\): row \(i\) aur column \(j\) ko cover kar dein, jo \(2 \times 2\) determinant bache woh minor hai, aur sign ka pattern \(+ - +\) hai. Sign wali ghalti sab se aam hai, is liye pattern yaad rakhein.

Row 2 ke cofactors
\[A_{21} = -\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(2 - 1) = -1\]
\[A_{22} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1 - 0) = -1\]
\[A_{23} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(1 - 0) = -1\]
Kyun: Row 2 mein sign pattern ulta hota hai: \(- + -\). Is liye \(A_{21}\) aur \(A_{23}\) mein minor ke aage minus lagta hai.

Row 3 ke cofactors
\[A_{31} = +\begin{vmatrix}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (4 - 1) = 3\]
\[A_{32} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-2 - 3) = 5\]
\[A_{33} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (1 + 6) = 7\]
Kyun: Row 3 ka pattern phir \(+ - +\) hai, bilkul row 1 jaisa.

Adjoint aur inverse
\[\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\]
\[A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A\) cofactors wale matrix ka transpose hai: row 1 ke cofactors column 1 mein jate hain, row 2 ke column 2 mein, aur row 3 ke column 3 mein. Fraction \(\frac{1}{|A|}\) ko bahar hi rehne dein, is se zarb aasaan rehti hai.

Zarb karein: \(X = A^{-1}B\)
\[X = \dfrac{1}{-2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & 7\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\]
Row ko column se zarb:
\[1(-1) + (-1)(4) + 3(1) = -2\]
\[3(-1) + (-1)(4) + 5(1) = -2\]
\[3(-1) + (-1)(4) + 7(1) = 0\]
\[X = \dfrac{1}{-2}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A \cdot B\) ka har entry \(\operatorname{adj}A\) ki ek row aur \(B\) ke column ka zarb hai (pehla pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se, phir jama). Aakhir mein har entry ko \(|A|\) se divide kiya.

Tasdeeq: teeno equations mein rakh kar dekhein
\[(1) - 2(1) + (0) = -1 \;\checkmark\]
\[3(1) + (1) - 2(0) = 4 \;\checkmark\]
\[(1) - (0) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Teeno equations poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Solve the following system of linear equations by matrix inversion method: \(2x_1 + x_2 + 3x_3 = 3\), \(x_1 + 3x_2 - 2x_3 = 0\), \(-3x_1 - x_2 + 2x_3 = 4\)
blocks.explanation:
Teen linear equations hain aur tareeqa pehle se tay hai: \(X = A^{-1}B\).
Teeno unknowns nikalne hain.
Plan: \(|A|\), phir nau (9) cofactors, \(\operatorname{adj}A\), \(A^{-1}\), phir \(B\) se zarb, aur aakhir mein tasdeeq.
Dhyan dein: \(X = A^{-1}B\) likhein, \(BA^{-1}\) nahi, kyunke matrix multiplication mein tarteeb badalne se jawab badal jata hai aur \(B\) \(3 \times 1\) hai, is liye \(BA^{-1}\) to ban hi nahi sakta. Cofactors ka sign pattern \(+ - +\), \(- + -\), \(+ - +\) yaad rakhein, aur adjoint banate waqt transpose lena na bhoolein: yeh do ghaltiyan exam mein sab se zyada hoti hain. Fraction \(\frac{1}{|A|}\) ko aakhir tak bahar rakhein, is se hisaab saaf rehta hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2x_1 + x_2 + 3x_3 = 3\), \(x_1 + 3x_2 - 2x_3 = 0\), \(-3x_1 - x_2 + 2x_3 = 4\)
Humein find karna hai: matrix inversion method se \(x_1, x_2, x_3\).
Tareeqa: System ko \(AX = B\) likhenge. Agar \(|A| \neq 0\) ho to dono taraf left se \(A^{-1}\) se zarb denge: \(A^{-1}AX = A^{-1}B\), yani \(X = A^{-1}B\). Inverse ke liye formula \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A\) use karenge.

System ko \(AX = B\) ki shakal mein likhein
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 \\ -3 & -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3\end{bmatrix},\ B = \begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki har row ek equation ke coefficients hain. Jo variable kisi equation mein maujood na ho, us ki jagah 0 likhna zaroori hai, warna matrix ghalat ban jata hai.

\(|A|\) nikalein
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & -2 \\ -3 & -1 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 2(6 - 2) - 1(2 - 6) + 3(-1 + 9)\]
\[= 8 + 4 + 24\]
\[= 36\]
Kyun: \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, is liye \(A^{-1}\) exist karta hai aur yeh method chalega.

Row 1 ke cofactors
\[A_{11} = +\begin{vmatrix}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (6 - 2) = 4\]
\[A_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & -2 \\ -3 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(2 - 6) = 4\]
\[A_{13} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ -3 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1 + 9) = 8\]
Kyun: \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\): row \(i\) aur column \(j\) ko cover kar dein, jo \(2 \times 2\) determinant bache woh minor hai, aur sign ka pattern \(+ - +\) hai. Sign wali ghalti sab se aam hai, is liye pattern yaad rakhein.

Row 2 ke cofactors
\[A_{21} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(2 + 3) = -5\]
\[A_{22} = +\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ -3 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (4 + 9) = 13\]
\[A_{23} = -\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-2 + 3) = -1\]
Kyun: Row 2 mein sign pattern ulta hota hai: \(- + -\). Is liye \(A_{21}\) aur \(A_{23}\) mein minor ke aage minus lagta hai.

Row 3 ke cofactors
\[A_{31} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 3 & -2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-2 - 9) = -11\]
\[A_{32} = -\begin{vmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-4 - 3) = 7\]
\[A_{33} = +\begin{vmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (6 - 1) = 5\]
Kyun: Row 3 ka pattern phir \(+ - +\) hai, bilkul row 1 jaisa.

Adjoint aur inverse
\[\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix}4 & -5 & -11 \\ 4 & 13 & 7 \\ 8 & -1 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]
\[A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{36}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -5 & -11 \\ 4 & 13 & 7 \\ 8 & -1 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A\) cofactors wale matrix ka transpose hai: row 1 ke cofactors column 1 mein jate hain, row 2 ke column 2 mein, aur row 3 ke column 3 mein. Fraction \(\frac{1}{|A|}\) ko bahar hi rehne dein, is se zarb aasaan rehti hai.

Zarb karein: \(X = A^{-1}B\)
\[X = \dfrac{1}{36}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -5 & -11 \\ 4 & 13 & 7 \\ 8 & -1 & 5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\]
Row ko column se zarb:
\[4(3) + (-5)(0) + (-11)(4) = -32\]
\[4(3) + 13(0) + 7(4) = 40\]
\[8(3) + (-1)(0) + 5(4) = 44\]
\[X = \dfrac{1}{36}\begin{bmatrix}-32 \\ 40 \\ 44\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-\frac{8}{9} \\ \frac{10}{9} \\ \frac{11}{9}\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A \cdot B\) ka har entry \(\operatorname{adj}A\) ki ek row aur \(B\) ke column ka zarb hai (pehla pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se, phir jama). Aakhir mein har entry ko \(|A|\) se divide kiya.

Tasdeeq: teeno equations mein rakh kar dekhein
\[2\left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) + \left(\frac{10}{9}\right) + 3\left(\frac{11}{9}\right) = 3 \;\checkmark\]
\[\left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) + 3\left(\frac{10}{9}\right) - 2\left(\frac{11}{9}\right) = 0 \;\checkmark\]
\[-3\left(-\frac{8}{9}\right) - \left(\frac{10}{9}\right) + 2\left(\frac{11}{9}\right) = 4 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Teeno equations poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Solve the following system of linear equations by matrix inversion method: \(x + y = 2\), \(2x - z = 1\), \(2y - 3z = -1\)
blocks.explanation:
Teen linear equations hain aur tareeqa pehle se tay hai: \(X = A^{-1}B\).
Teeno unknowns nikalne hain.
Plan: \(|A|\), phir nau (9) cofactors, \(\operatorname{adj}A\), \(A^{-1}\), phir \(B\) se zarb, aur aakhir mein tasdeeq.
Dhyan dein: \(X = A^{-1}B\) likhein, \(BA^{-1}\) nahi, kyunke matrix multiplication mein tarteeb badalne se jawab badal jata hai aur \(B\) \(3 \times 1\) hai, is liye \(BA^{-1}\) to ban hi nahi sakta. Cofactors ka sign pattern \(+ - +\), \(- + -\), \(+ - +\) yaad rakhein, aur adjoint banate waqt transpose lena na bhoolein: yeh do ghaltiyan exam mein sab se zyada hoti hain. Fraction \(\frac{1}{|A|}\) ko aakhir tak bahar rakhein, is se hisaab saaf rehta hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(x + y = 2\), \(2x - z = 1\), \(2y - 3z = -1\)
Humein find karna hai: matrix inversion method se \(x, y, z\).
Tareeqa: System ko \(AX = B\) likhenge. Agar \(|A| \neq 0\) ho to dono taraf left se \(A^{-1}\) se zarb denge: \(A^{-1}AX = A^{-1}B\), yani \(X = A^{-1}B\). Inverse ke liye formula \(A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A\) use karenge.

System ko \(AX = B\) ki shakal mein likhein
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3\end{bmatrix}\]
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix},\ B = \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki har row ek equation ke coefficients hain. Jo variable kisi equation mein maujood na ho, us ki jagah 0 likhna zaroori hai, warna matrix ghalat ban jata hai.

\(|A|\) nikalein
\[|A| = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= 1(0 + 2) - 1(-6 - 0) + 0(4 - 0)\]
\[= 2 + 6 + 0\]
\[= 8\]
Kyun: \(|A| \neq 0\) hai, is liye \(A^{-1}\) exist karta hai aur yeh method chalega.

Row 1 ke cofactors
\[A_{11} = +\begin{vmatrix}0 & -1 \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (0 + 2) = 2\]
\[A_{12} = -\begin{vmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 0 & -3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-6 - 0) = 6\]
\[A_{13} = +\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (4 - 0) = 4\]
Kyun: \(A_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j}M_{ij}\): row \(i\) aur column \(j\) ko cover kar dein, jo \(2 \times 2\) determinant bache woh minor hai, aur sign ka pattern \(+ - +\) hai. Sign wali ghalti sab se aam hai, is liye pattern yaad rakhein.

Row 2 ke cofactors
\[A_{21} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-3 - 0) = 3\]
\[A_{22} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-3 - 0) = -3\]
\[A_{23} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(2 - 0) = -2\]
Kyun: Row 2 mein sign pattern ulta hota hai: \(- + -\). Is liye \(A_{21}\) aur \(A_{23}\) mein minor ke aage minus lagta hai.

Row 3 ke cofactors
\[A_{31} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (-1 - 0) = -1\]
\[A_{32} = -\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -(-1 - 0) = 1\]
\[A_{33} = +\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix}\]
\[= (0 - 2) = -2\]
Kyun: Row 3 ka pattern phir \(+ - +\) hai, bilkul row 1 jaisa.

Adjoint aur inverse
\[\operatorname{adj}A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]
\[A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{8}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A\) cofactors wale matrix ka transpose hai: row 1 ke cofactors column 1 mein jate hain, row 2 ke column 2 mein, aur row 3 ke column 3 mein. Fraction \(\frac{1}{|A|}\) ko bahar hi rehne dein, is se zarb aasaan rehti hai.

Zarb karein: \(X = A^{-1}B\)
\[X = \dfrac{1}{8}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 & -2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}\]
Row ko column se zarb:
\[2(2) + 3(1) + (-1)(-1) = 8\]
\[6(2) + (-3)(1) + 1(-1) = 8\]
\[4(2) + (-2)(1) + (-2)(-1) = 8\]
\[X = \dfrac{1}{8}\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ 8 \\ 8\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(\operatorname{adj}A \cdot B\) ka har entry \(\operatorname{adj}A\) ki ek row aur \(B\) ke column ka zarb hai (pehla pehle se, doosra doosre se, teesra teesre se, phir jama). Aakhir mein har entry ko \(|A|\) se divide kiya.

Tasdeeq: teeno equations mein rakh kar dekhein
\[(1) + (1) = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[2(1) - (1) = 1 \;\checkmark\]
\[2(1) - 3(1) = -1 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Teeno equations poori ho gayin, is liye jawab sahi hai.
